description: What Private Mode may download, from where, and how it is verified. sha256 values are filled by `npm run models:pin` on a machine with network access; until then the manager refuses to install.

models.label: Distilled emotion classifier (on-device)
models.honest_note: A distilled ~66M-parameter classifier. It is less accurate than the server model it stands in for, it labels tone rather than diagnosis, and it never decides safety.

models.label: Distilled crisis-signal classifier (not shipped yet)
models.honest_note: No distilled self-harm classifier is pinned. A general toxicity model is not a substitute and would mislabel risk, so this slot stays empty: the deterministic rules engine is the safety layer, and models may only ever raise caution.

models.label: Small on-device language model (WebGPU)
models.honest_note: This build does not name an on-device language model, so replies come from the reviewed templates instead. An operator names one with PRIVATE_LLM_MODEL_ID (see .env.example) and re-runs `npm run models:manifest`. Whichever model that turns out to be, it is smaller than the server model: replies are shorter, plainer and less flexible, and every one of them still passes the on-device output guard.
